categoryMeta.description: Marathon workouts focused on long runs, steady endurance, marathon effort, and fueling practice.

workouts.title: Marathon Easy Long Run Foundation
workouts.summary: A controlled easy long run for building marathon time-on-feet without added intensity.
workouts.riskReason: Long duration increases cumulative fatigue, hydration demand, and lower-leg stress.

intensityGuide.paceGuide: Use marathon effort, steady effort, or easy conversational effort. Do not chase fixed pace if terrain, heat, or fatigue changes.
intensityGuide.hrGuide: Heart rate should rise gradually; sustained drift late in long runs is a sign to slow down, fuel, or shorten.

warmup.name: Easy Start
warmup.description: Start with easy jogging or brisk walking before settling into the main endurance work.
notes: Let the first minutes feel almost too easy.

mainSet.name: 90–120-Min Easy Long Run
mainSet.description: Run continuously at easy conversational effort.
notes: Fuel if the run exceeds 90 minutes.

cooldown.name: Easy Walk-Jog Cooldown
cooldown.description: Walk or jog very easily after the main endurance work.
notes: Rehydrate and let breathing return to normal.

easier.description: Reduce the main-set load while keeping the same training purpose.

mainSet.name: 75–90-Min Easy Long Run
mainSet.description: Run continuously at easy effort for a shorter duration.
notes: Keep it relaxed.

harder.description: Increase the main-set load only when the base version is controlled.

mainSet.name: 120–140-Min Easy Long Run
mainSet.description: Run continuously at easy effort for a longer duration.
notes: Practice fueling.

coachingNotes: Use effort and fueling execution as the success metric, not only average pace.
Keep the first half conservative so late running mechanics stay clean.
Practice the same shoes, socks, hydration, and fueling approach you might use on race day when relevant.
commonMistakes: Turning marathon effort into threshold effort.
Waiting too long before taking fuel or fluid during long sessions.
Forcing pace when heat, hills, or fatigue clearly change the effort.
safetyNotes: Stop or shorten the workout if pain changes your stride.
Carry fluids or plan access to water for longer sessions.
Avoid demanding marathon workouts when sick, under-slept, injured, or carrying heavy fatigue.

shareCard.purposeText: A controlled easy long run for building marathon time-on-feet without added intensity.
